note: Issue #108/#192 costmap-silhouette capture. Live `openral deploy sim` graph (slam + nav2 + octomap, reasoner on, no policy dispatched) on q-laptop / RTX 5070 Laptop, ROS 2 Jazzy, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp. One graph launch per scene, each at its pinned seed. Nav2 driven by a single direct NavigateToPose goal 2.0 m ahead in `map`, so the base translates and both rolling windows sweep new geometry. Produced by `tools/_nav2_costmap_silhouette_probe.py`: every cell centre of every published Costmap is transformed into base_link and tested against the manifest's bare chassis polygon (`base_footprint_polygon`) plus any attached primitives, using `payload_scan_filter_node`'s own containment predicates. `total_marked_in_silhouette` counts cells at exactly LETHAL_OBSTACLE (254) - not 253, which is what an inflation layer writes near a legitimate obstacle somewhere else.

finding: The GLOBAL costmap is EMPTY on both scenes: max cost 0 over 50 and 51 published samples, zero non-zero cells at any point, while the LOCAL costmap on the same graph peaks at 254 with 1988 / 1053 non-zero cells. Its `obstacle_layer` is configured on the same filtered `/openral/nav2/scan` the local costmap's `voxel_layer` reads, `static_layer` is deliberately out of its plugin chain (rolling window, SLAM-from-scratch), and `planner_server` logs no warning of any kind. NavfnPlanner therefore planned the accepted NavigateToPose goal against a blank 20x20 m grid. Not what #192 set out to measure, not fixed here, and it makes the GLOBAL half of the silhouette verdict VACUOUS - nothing is marked inside the robot because nothing is marked at all. The LOCAL half is non-vacuous and is the result this file records.

caveat: Two attribution limits, stated so the numbers are not over-read. (1) `openral_sim.backends.robocasa.synthesize_laser_scan_2d` re-casts through the robot's own MuJoCo kinematic tree, so a self-return never enters /scan in sim in the first place. A clean silhouette here is the END STATE being correct; it is not proof that payload_scan_filter_node is what made it so. That attribution is what the deterministic sweep in tests/integration/test_nav2_scan_filter_live.py exists for - it ships a control that fails. (2) attached_objects stayed 0 on both runs (no policy was dispatched, so nothing was ever grasped), so the PAYLOAD half of the silhouette is unmeasured and is reported as payload_silhouette_measured: false rather than as a clean verdict.
